$comment: Project-scoped MCP servers for WeVolunteer. Committed deliberately, so the
restricted configuration is the default a developer gets rather than
something each person has to remember to apply.
NO CREDENTIALS HERE. Better Stack authenticates by browser OAuth on first
use; Claude Code stores the resulting token outside the repository. A Better
Stack API token must never be added to this file.
X-MCP-Tools-Only is an ALLOWLIST, and it is DEFENCE IN DEPTH — NOT the
security boundary. The boundary is the Better Stack ROLE of the account that
authenticates here, because that is what Better Stack enforces server-side.
Three things about the header are still unverified, and each of them is a way
for it to be worth less than it looks:
1. Only three of these tokens (monitors, monitor, incidents) come from
Better Stack's own documented example. The rest are inferred from the
tool categories in their docs and are UNVERIFIED — the tool list is not
readable without authenticating.
2. Whether an unrecognised token is ignored (safe: fewer tools) or voids
the header (unsafe: all tools) is not documented.
3. Whether a token matches a tool NAME exactly or as a category PREFIX is
not documented — and it decides whether an entry admits one read tool or
every tool in that category, writes included.
The singular 'monitor' from Better Stack's example is deliberately NOT in the
list below because of (3). If matching is exact it is a read tool and its
absence costs one lookup; if matching is a prefix it is the entry that admits
monitor-create and monitor-delete. Losing a lookup is an inconvenience;
handing an agent the ability to delete an alerting monitor is an outage that
nobody would be paged about. Restore it once the audit answers (3).
To answer all three from the live service in about a minute:
BETTERSTACK_API_TOKEN=... node bin/betterstack-mcp-audit.mjs
It only ever sends initialize and tools/list — it never calls a tool. Record
what it finds in docs/operations/betterstack.md, and until then do not let
Claude Code authenticate here as a Better Stack Admin. Run /mcp after
connecting to see which tools actually came through.
